title: Affine smooth isomorphism scheme of two represented torsors over an arbitrary base
statement: Let $B$ and $Y$ be schemes, with a morphism $Y\to B$ [def-pc-scheme]. Let $H\to B$ be an affine smooth group scheme [pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]: its multiplication, identity and inverse obey the diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme], with base $B$. Let $P,Q\to Y$ be represented right $H$-torsors [def-sfb-split-solvable-right-torsors], using base $B$. For each $Y$-scheme $f:T\to Y$ put $P_T=P\times_YT$, $Q_T=Q\times_YT$ and $H_T=H\times_BT$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $\mathcal I(T)$ be the set of $T$-scheme isomorphisms $P_T\simeq Q_T$ commuting with the right $H_T$-actions, with pullback as restriction. This functor is represented by a $Y$-scheme $I=\underline{\operatorname{Isom}}_{H,Y}(P,Q)$: naturally in every $T\to Y$ there is a bijection $\operatorname{Mor}_Y(T,I)\cong\mathcal I(T)$. The morphism $I\to Y$ is affine and smooth. In particular, if $Y$ is affine, then $I$ is an affine scheme. No field base, triviality of the torsors, connectedness or reductivity of $H$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 049C (remark-fun-with-torsors), affine torsor representability; descent.tex Tags 0245 (lemma-affine) and 02VL (lemma-descending-property-smooth). Agent-extracted isomorphism-functor version via simultaneous fppf trivializations; also the affine smooth Isom input of Alper--Halpern-Leistner--Heinloth, Section 2 Claim 3, printed p.3 (WANTED locally).

proof.text: Put $W=P\times_YQ$, with tautological sections $p\in P(W)$ and $q\in Q(W)$. The represented-torsor definition makes $P\to Y$ and $Q\to Y$ flat, surjective and finitely presented, hence singleton fppf covers. By fppf-to-fpqc inclusion and the base-change and composition axioms for fpqc coverings, $Q_P=W\to P\to Y$ gives the singleton fpqc cover $W\to Y$. Its pullback $T_W\to T$ is an fpqc cover for every $T\to Y$.

The torsor isomorphism $(x,h)\mapsto(x,xh)$, pulled back along $p$ and $q$, identifies $P_W$ and $Q_W$ with $H_W$ by $h\mapsto ph$ and $h\mapsto qh$. These are scheme isomorphisms: the inverse sends $x$ to the unique $h$ with $x=ph$, using the inverse of the torsor isomorphism. For every $W$-scheme $T$, an equivariant isomorphism is therefore uniquely $ph\mapsto qch$ for a section $c\in H_W(T)$; its inverse is $qh\mapsto pc^{-1}h$. Evaluation at $p$ gives the inverse correspondence. All formulas use the group-scheme multiplication and inverse, so are morphisms and commute with every base change.

source.place: Tag 049C (remark-fun-with-torsors), explicit simultaneous trivialization argument for right torsors.

proof.text: Over $W_2=W\times_YW$, write the two tautological pairs as $(p_1,q_1)$ and $(p_2,q_2)$. The torsor isomorphisms give unique scheme sections $a,b$ of $H_{W_2}$ with $p_2=p_1a$, $q_2=q_1b$. The same equivariant isomorphism has coefficients related by $c_2=b^{-1}c_1a$. Thus $\varphi(c)=b^{-1}ca$ is an isomorphism between the two pullbacks of $H_W$, with inverse $c\mapsto bca^{-1}$. On $W_3$, uniqueness gives $a_{13}=a_{12}a_{23}$ and $b_{13}=b_{12}b_{23}$; hence $b_{23}^{-1}(b_{12}^{-1}ca_{12})a_{23}=b_{13}^{-1}ca_{13}$. This proves the descent cocycle. Since $H_W\to W$ is a base change of the affine morphism $H\to B$, affine effective descent gives a scheme $I\to Y$ and $I\times_YW\simeq H_W$ inducing precisely $\varphi$.

source.place: Tag 0245 (lemma-affine); groupoids.tex Tag 049C, with the explicit right-torsor cocycle.

proof.text: Fix $T\to Y$. Apply morphism descent to the singleton fpqc cover $T_W\to T$: a section of $I_T$ is exactly a section of $H_{T_W}$ whose two pullbacks obey $c_2=b^{-1}c_1a$, by the defining comparison for $I$. Such coefficients give local equivariant isomorphisms $ph\mapsto qch$. The transition formula says exactly that their two pullbacks agree as maps $P_{T_W}\to Q_{T_W}$. Morphism descent, now for the two $T$-schemes $P_T,Q_T$, gives a unique map $u:P_T\to Q_T$. Descend the local inverses too; faithfulness in morphism descent shows both composites are identities. It also shows equivariance by comparing the two maps $P_T\times_T H_T\to Q_T$, which agree after the same cover. Conversely an equivariant isomorphism pulls back to a unique local coefficient by step 2; step 3 forces its transition relation, so it descends to a unique section of $I_T$. These operations are inverse. For $T\prime\to T$, their pullbacks agree with the same local formulas, so uniqueness of descent proves naturality. Thus $\operatorname{Mor}_Y(T,I)\cong\mathcal I(T)$ for all $T$.

source.place: Tag 02W0 (lemma-refine-coverings-fully-faithful), last assertion; topologies.tex Tag 022D for the test-scheme covers.

proof.text: The base change $I_W\to W$ is isomorphic to $H_W\to W$, which is affine by base change of $H\to B$. The singleton $W\to Y$ is an fpqc cover by step 1. Affineness descends along this cover, giving $I\to Y$ affine. If $Y$ is affine, the source of this affine morphism is an affine scheme.

By smooth base change, $H_W\to W$ is smooth, and hence so is $I_W\to W$. Descend first along $Q_P=W\to P$: it is flat and surjective because it is the base change of the fpqc cover $Q\to Y$ (step 1 and the covering definition), and it is quasi-compact by quasi-compact base change since the torsor $Q\to Y$ is finitely presented. Single-cover smooth descent therefore makes $I_P\to P$ smooth. Descend again along $P\to Y$, which is flat, surjective and quasi-compact by the represented-torsor definition. This gives smoothness of $I\to Y$. These applications require no field hypothesis or trivialization over $Y$ itself.

lean.statement: theorem isom_affine_smooth {B : Scheme.{u}} (H : Grp (Over B)) [IsAffineHom H.X.hom] [Smooth H.X.hom] (Y : Over B) (P Q : RepresentedRightTorsor H Y) : ∃ I : Over Y, IsAffineHom I.hom.left ∧ Smooth I.hom.left ∧ (IsAffine Y.left → IsAffine I.left.left) ∧ ∃ E : ∀ T : Over Y, (T ⟶ I) ≃ EquivariantIsom P Q T.hom, ∀ (T T' : Over Y) (h : T' ⟶ T) (s : T ⟶ I), (E T' (h ≫ s)).iso.hom ≫ testChangeMap Q h = testChangeMap P h ≫ (E T s).iso.hom
